task: Face detection. Graded two ways on real frames: recall - every face a human can see must be found, and its box must agree with the platform's own already-`production` face detector (insightface-buffalo-l-detect / SCRFD) at IoU >= 0.5 on the same frame; and false positives - frames with no human face in them at all must return zero detections.

tolerance.note: IoU is measured against SCRFD's own box, not a hand-drawn ground truth: SCRFD is already `production` in this registry and independently validated, so it is the best real reference available here, and two detectors from unrelated architecture families agreeing on a box location is meaningful evidence that both decoded the frame correctly. It is NOT a claim that SCRFD's box is pixel-perfect truth.

note: CenterFace is anchor-free (CenterNet-style), despite being grouped with the two anchor-based detectors in CHECKLIST.md's own risk tiering - established by reading the real reference source, not assumed from the grouping. Its specific silent-failure risks are the log-space box scale and the (dy, dx) landmark pair order, both of which this golden set exercises indirectly: a swapped landmark order still lands inside the box on a roughly-square face, so the real check is that the 5 points agree positionally with SCRFD's own 5 points, which is recorded in the run's per-image results.

unmeasured: Landmark ACCURACY. Structurally correct and positionally close to SCRFD's own points on the real faces, but no hand-labelled 5-point ground truth exists in this repo, so landmark error is not scored.

Rotated-face behaviour. The reference implementation's own note says CenterFace landmark accuracy degrades past roughly 20-30 degrees of in-plane rotation; both faces here are upright, so that limit is inherited-and-documented, not measured.
Night/IR recall - the night frame here is a negative control with no face in it.
